cases.situation: My son Eli (Year 8) got a zero on his science project for being 'late', but Google Classroom shows he submitted it Sunday night before the Monday deadline. Teacher is Mr Barnes.
cases.reply: Hi Mr Barnes, I'm Eli Carter's dad (8C). Eli's science project was marked late with a zero, but Google Classroom shows he submitted it at 7:40pm on Sunday 20 September, before the Monday deadline; screenshot attached. Could you take a look and let me know if I've missed something? Thanks for checking, Daniel Carter
cases.note: A question, not a verdict: the timestamp does the arguing, and 'if I've missed something' lets him fix it without losing face.

cases.situation: 女儿三年级，最近每天晚上写数学作业写到十点，一边写一边哭，说听不懂。班主任兼数学老师是张老师。
cases.reply: 张老师您好，我是三年级二班刘可欣的妈妈。可欣最近两周数学作业经常写到晚上十点，边写边哭，说两位数乘法课上没太听懂。想问问您在课堂上有没有观察到类似的情况？我们在家每天陪她练15分钟口算。您这周哪天方便通个电话？放学后或中午都可以。谢谢您！
cases.note: 只说看到的事实，再问老师看到了什么，不先下结论说作业太多。

cases.situation: Emailed my son's teacher Ms Rivera on Sept 14 and Sept 21 about a kid shoving him in the bus line, twice leaving a bruise. No reply either time. Want to go to the assistant principal, Mr Grant.
cases.reply:
Dear Mr Grant,
I'm writing about my son Noah Kim (4th grade, Ms Rivera's class). Since early September another student has been shoving him in the bus line after school, twice leaving a bruise on his arm. I emailed Ms Rivera on 14 and 21 September (copies below) and haven't heard back, and it's still happening. Could you let me know the school's next steps, and when we could meet this week?
Thank you,
Grace Kim
cases.note: Escalate with dates and copies, no criticism of the teacher. If Noah is being hurt again, contact the safeguarding lead the same day.

cases.situation: My daughter Nora (Grade 5, Ms. Kowalski's class) was just diagnosed with ADHD. She says she can't focus in her seat by the window and keeps getting in trouble for unfinished work. I'd like to talk to the teacher before the November conferences.
cases.reply: Hi Ms. Kowalski, I'm Nora Brennan's dad. Nora was recently diagnosed with ADHD, and she's told us she finds it hard to focus in her seat by the window and often doesn't finish classwork. I'd really like to hear what you've seen in class before we assume anything. At home we've started breaking homework into 15-minute blocks with short breaks, which seems to help. Could we meet for 20 minutes in the next couple of weeks? I'm free after 3:30 any day, or happy to do a call. Thank you.
cases.note: Share the diagnosis only as far as it helps the teacher, then ask what she sees instead of prescribing a seat change in the first message.

cases.situation: My son Kai (Year 10) got a Saturday detention for 'defiance' after refusing to take his hoodie off in class on Monday. He has an eczema flare on his arms and was embarrassed. Head of year is Mr Okafor; detention is this Saturday, Oct 3.
cases.reply: Dear Mr Okafor, I'm Kai Tanaka's mum (10B). Kai has a Saturday detention on 3 October for refusing to take off his hoodie in class on Monday. He has an eczema flare on his arms at the moment and was embarrassed to show it, which he should have explained rather than just refusing. Could the detention be reconsidered, and could he wear a plain long-sleeved top under his blazer until it clears? I can send a note from his GP, and I'm free to talk any afternoon this week. Thank you, Emi Tanaka
cases.note: Disagreeing with a sanction: give the missing fact, concede Kai's part, and ask for a decision plus a practical fix.

cases.situation: I emailed my daughter Mia's Grade 7 teacher, Mr. Hale, that she's spending 3 hours a night on homework. He replied the assignments are designed for 45 minutes and maybe she's distracted at home. I don't want a fight.
cases.reply: Thanks for getting back to me so quickly, Mr. Hale, that's useful to know, 45 minutes is a lot less than we're seeing. This week I'll keep a simple log of what Mia works on and for how long, with her phone in the kitchen, and send it to you on Friday. If it's still well over, could we meet for 15 minutes next week to see where she's getting stuck?
cases.note: Don't argue with the implied criticism; turn it into shared evidence and a small next step.

cases.situation: 儿子乐乐上四年级，10月15号、16号（周四周五）要回老家参加外婆八十大寿，得请两天假。班主任是李老师。想提前说一声，也问问落下的功课怎么补。
cases.reply: 李老师您好，我是四年级三班王乐乐的妈妈。乐乐外婆10月17日过八十大寿，我们要回老家一趟，想给他请10月15日周四和16日周五两天假，19日周一正常上学。想问一下这两天的作业和课堂内容，能不能麻烦您提前告诉我们，或者让同桌帮忙记一下？我们会在路上带着他补上。给您添麻烦了，谢谢！
cases.note: 计划中的请假要提前说，给出准确日期和返校日，再主动问怎么补课，老师更好安排。

cases.situation: My ex and I separated over the summer and our son Sam (Year 3, Mr Doyle's class) now lives with me Monday to Wednesday. All the school emails and reading-record notes go only to his mum. I want to be copied in, and give the teacher a heads-up.
cases.reply: Hi Mr Doyle, I'm Sam Reid's dad (3D). Sam's mum and I separated over the summer, and Sam is now with me Monday to Wednesday and with her the rest of the week. Could you add me to the class emails and reading-record notes, at tom.reid@example.com, so both homes stay in the loop? He seems to be handling it well, and we're keeping homework and bedtimes the same at both houses. If you notice anything in class, I'd really appreciate hearing about it. Thanks, Tom Reid
cases.note: Family change: facts only, no blame on the other parent, one practical ask, and an open door for the teacher to share what she sees.

cases.situation: My son Owen's teacher, Ms. Delgado (Grade 2), called and then emailed me yesterday: Owen pushed a classmate off the slide at recess and the boy scraped his knee. Owen says the other kid pushed him first. I want to reply to her email without sounding defensive.
cases.reply:
Hi Ms. Delgado, thank you for calling me yesterday about recess. We talked with Owen last night. He says the other boy pushed him first, and he also agrees that pushing someone off the slide is never okay; he's written a short sorry note he'd like to give him. If you saw anything that would help us understand what happened, I'd be grateful to hear it. Could we have a quick call this week about what Owen should do next time he's upset at recess? I'm free after 3:30 any day.
Thanks,
Laura Kemp
cases.note: When your child is the one in trouble, don't argue the facts: show what you're doing at home, ask what the teacher saw, and look ahead.

cases.situation: My daughter Ava (Year 9) was moved from top set maths to set 2 this week. She's upset, mostly because nobody told her why. Her maths teacher is Mr Singh. I want to ask about it without sounding like I'm demanding she be moved back.
cases.reply: Hi Mr Singh, I'm Ava Morgan's mum (9R). Ava told me she's moved from set 1 to set 2 in maths this week, and she's quite upset, mainly because she isn't sure why. Could you tell me what the move was based on, and what she'd need to show to move back up? We're happy to work on it at home. I can do a call any day after 4pm this week. Thank you.
cases.note: Question a placement by asking what it was based on and what the route back looks like, not by asking for a reversal.

cases.situation: My daughter Maya (Year 9) showed me a class group chat where two classmates shared an edited photo of her with nasty captions. It started Sunday night and has been screenshotted into other chats. The school's safeguarding lead is Mrs Ellis.
cases.reply: Dear Mrs Ellis, I'm writing with a safeguarding concern about my daughter, Maya Grant, in Year 9. Since Sunday evening an edited photo of Maya with unkind captions has been shared in a class group chat and screenshotted into other chats; I've saved copies and can send them today. Maya is very distressed. Could you let me know the school's process, and could we speak today or tomorrow? At home we've reported the posts to the app and she's off the chat for now. I'm on 07700 900 461 all day. Thank you, Rachel Grant
cases.note: Online bullying goes straight to the safeguarding lead: dates, evidence on offer, a question about process and a prompt time frame, without naming the other children yet.

cases.situation: My son Jonah (Year 5, Ms Carter's class) keeps saying he finishes his maths work early and then gets bored, and he's been told off twice this month for chatting. I don't want to come across as the pushy 'my kid is gifted' parent.
cases.reply: Hi Ms Carter, I'm Jonah Price's dad (5C). Jonah has mentioned a few times this month that he often finishes his maths early and isn't sure what to do next, and I suspect that's when the chatting happens. Have you noticed the same thing? If so, could there be an extension task he moves on to when he's done? At home we do a bit of puzzle maths at weekends, which he loves. I'm free for a quick call after 4pm any day. Thanks, Ben Price
cases.note: Ask what she sees before proposing a fix, and own the chatting rather than excusing it.

cases.situation: 儿子陈浩刚上一年级，对花生严重过敏，医生开了肾上腺素笔。班主任是周老师，听说下周学校组织秋游还会发零食，我想提前跟老师说清楚。
cases.reply: 周老师您好，我是一年级（2）班陈浩的妈妈。浩浩对花生严重过敏，医生说哪怕一点点也可能引起严重反应，他的肾上腺素笔放在书包侧袋里，医院证明和用法说明我明天让他带给您。听说下周秋游会发零食，想问一下学校对过敏的孩子有没有固定的处理流程？我可以单独给他准备一份零食。您哪天放学后方便，我当面跟您演示一下笔怎么用。谢谢您！
cases.note: 健康安全的事要具体：过敏原、严重程度、药放在哪，再问学校的流程，并主动分担。

cases.situation: 女儿朵朵读五年级，学校下个月去杭州研学三天，费用1680元，这周五前要交。我最近失业了，一下子拿不出来，但不想让孩子知道，也不想在家长群里问。班主任是吴老师。
cases.reply: 吴老师您好，我是五年级（3）班林朵朵的妈妈。想私下跟您了解一下，这次杭州研学的1680元，学校有没有分期交或者困难补助的办法？我家最近情况有些变化，一次交齐有点困难，但很希望朵朵能去。这件事麻烦您先不要跟孩子提。您方便的时候回我一下就好，谢谢您！
cases.note: 费用的事私下问，只问学校有没有办法，不必解释家里的细节，更不要在群里问。

cases.situation: Ma fille Inès (CM1) m'a raconté que sa maîtresse, Mme Lefèvre, a dit devant toute la classe que son exposé était « nul ». Depuis, Inès ne veut plus aller à l'école le matin. Je veux en parler sans attaquer l'enseignante.
cases.reply: Bonjour Madame Lefèvre, je suis la maman d'Inès Moreau (CM1). Inès est rentrée très touchée après son exposé sur les volcans : elle m'a dit que vous l'aviez trouvé « nul » devant la classe, et depuis elle a du mal à partir à l'école le matin. Je sais que je n'ai que sa version, alors j'aimerais savoir comment vous avez vécu ce moment. Pourriez-vous m'accorder un quart d'heure cette semaine ? Je suis disponible tous les jours après 16 h 30. Merci beaucoup, Claire Moreau
cases.note: Quand le souci vient de l'enseignante : les faits tels que l'enfant les raconte, la question plutôt que le verdict, et pas la direction en copie.

cases.situation: We moved from Brazil to Leeds in September. Our son Davi (Year 6, Miss Hart's class) speaks only a little English and says he eats lunch alone most days. He loves football and drawing, and we read an English picture book with him every night.
cases.reply: Hi Miss Hart, I'm Davi Souza's mum (Year 6). We moved here from Brazil in September, and Davi is still learning English. He tells me he eats lunch on his own most days. He loves football and drawing, which might be an easy way for him to join in with other children. Could you tell me how the school usually supports children who are new to English, and could we meet for 15 minutes one afternoon? At home we read an English picture book together every night. Thank you, Juliana Souza
cases.note: New arrival: share what helps the child, ask about the school's usual support rather than prescribing it.

cases.situation: My son Yusuf (Year 7, form tutor Ms Lawson) will fast for Ramadan for the first time this coming February. He's proud and a bit nervous about it. He has PE on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and we're doing a few practice fasts at weekends so he knows how he feels. I want to ask early how the school handles it.
cases.reply: Hi Ms Lawson, I'm Yusuf Rahman's mum (7L). Yusuf will be fasting during Ramadan for the first time this coming February, and he's proud and a little nervous about it. He has PE on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so I wanted to ask early how the school usually supports pupils who are fasting, for example with PE and where he can go at lunchtime. At home we're doing a few practice fasts at weekends so he knows how he feels. Could you let me know, or point me to the right person? Thank you, Samira Rahman
cases.note: Asking months ahead, and asking about the school's usual approach rather than prescribing one, makes it an easy yes.
